newsitem.title: TURKEY: Early June rains please Turk farmers after dry May.
newsitem.headline: Early June rains please Turk farmers after dry May.

text.p: Recent heavy rains in June have ended Turkish farmers' fears that a dry May would lead to deterioration in the quantity and quality in their crop, farm officials said.
They said Turkey's central regions had received as much rain in the first eight days of June as they did in the whole June last year.
One official said the May rains were less than seasonal averages.
Officials estimated in May that Turkey's 1997/98 wheat output would be less than the government's target of 18 million tonnes. Turkey produced 16.5 million tonnes in 1996/97.
Wheat harvesting began in southern regions of Turkey in late-May.
Weather officials said rains in central Turkey, expected to produce three million tonnes of grain this year, would continue until mid-June.
